1. Outside view. Historically, presidential job approval is relatively stable, moving only 1-2 points week-to-week unless driven by a major event. In the three provided weeks, "strongly approve" dropped steadily: 22.0 -> 19.0 -> 17.0, an average drop of 2.5 points per week. A naive linear extrapolation would predict a value of 14.5 to 15.0 for the next release. 

2. Inside view. According to the search results, the Economist/YouGov poll conducted Sept. 18-21 saw Trump's overall approval rating drop 5 points in a single week among registered voters (from 40% to 35%). Since "strongly approve" tends to constitute roughly half of the overall approval (and we know it was 17.0 when overall was 40%), a 5-point drop in total approval will likely drag "strongly approve" down by at least 1-3 points. A further drop to 14.0-16.0% is highly probable, maintaining the recent downward momentum before finding a natural floor.

3. Pre-mortem. What if the forecast is wrong? The most likely reason would be that the upcoming scheduled release (Sept. 29) captures a new polling wave (Sept. 25-28) that exhibits mean reversion, bouncing the overall approval rating back up to 37-38% and bringing "strongly approve" back to ~17%. Conversely, if the drop in the Sept. 18-21 poll was driven heavily by his base abandoning him, strongly approve could plunge even further to ~13%. I will set an SD that comfortably captures a rebound to 17% or a further slide to 13%.

4. Calibrate. Given the prior moves of 3.0 and 2.0 points, expecting a move of 1.0 to 2.5 points makes sense. Centering the mean at 15.3 with a standard deviation of 1.5 gives a 68% confidence interval of roughly [13.8, 16.8], encompassing both continued decay and slight mean reversion.
